description: Compare two tire sizes (e.g. 205/55R16 vs 225/45R17): overall diameter, circumference, revolutions per km and speedometer error.

faqs.q: How do I read a tire size like 205/55R16?
faqs.a: 205 is the tread width in mm, 55 is the aspect ratio (sidewall height as a percentage of width), R means radial construction, and 16 is the wheel rim diameter in inches.
Your speedometer is calibrated to the old tire's circumference. True speed = indicated speed × (new circumference ÷ old circumference). A larger new tire makes the speedo read low.

faqs.q: How much diameter change is safe?
faqs.a: Most manufacturers recommend staying within ±3% of the original overall diameter to keep gearing, clearance and speedometer accuracy safe.
